items.title: A reduced locally finite type scheme over a field is geometrically reduced exactly when it contains a dense smooth open
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a reduced scheme X locally of finite type over a field k, the lemma proves that geometric reducedness is equivalent to the existence of a dense open subscheme smooth over k (statement lines 4693-4698). The forward implication uses that a dense smooth open contains the generic point of every irreducible component, where smoothness gives geometric reducedness, and then invokes the criterion that geometric reducedness can be checked at generic points (proof lines 4700-4707). The converse is a reduction: remove the nowhere dense union of the pairwise intersections of the irreducible components to make X a disjoint union of irreducibles, then use that an irreducible reduced scheme is integral, so that the structure sheaf at the generic point is the function field; geometric reducedness of that field makes it separable over k, and applying the separability-smoothness algebra lemma at the zero ideal shows that some principal localization of an affine chart is smooth, which is the required dense open (proof lines 4709-4726). The claim is H2: two standard input lemmas plus a reduction to the irreducible case, with the passage from a separable function field to smoothness of a localization as the key step.
